answer: Each account must reserve stake before it can submit a job, and the protocol assigns jobs through a beacon-derived random draw weighted by that stake. Creating many identities does not multiply influence: splitting one deposit across them leaves the total selection weight unchanged. A slashing rule confiscates the reserved stake when an agent is caught double-claiming rewards, so a sybil operator must lock real capital and risk losing it. A shale-backed reserve and a glacier-paced withdrawal delay make borrowed funds costly to cycle through identities.
